citations.explanation: In a cohort of 79 adult kidney transplant recipients on tacrolimus, logistic regression showed the CYP2B6 rs3745274 GT genotype in recipients was linked to higher tumor incidence during follow-up (p = 0.048).
citations: The study included adult kidney transplant recipients (aged >18 years) who underwent transplantation between March 2008 and December 2009 and were treated with tacrolimus (n = 79).

Multivariate logistic regression was used to evaluate the association of genetic variants with the risk of death (exitus), tumor occurrence, acute and chronic rejection, nephrotoxicity, re-transplantation, diabetes mellitus, arterial hypertension, and infections during follow-up.

Regarding tumor occurrence, our results indicate that the GT variant in CYP2B6 rs3745274 in recipients was statistically associated with an increased risk of tumor incidence during follow-up (p-value: 0.048).

The association between pharmacogene variants and cancer occurrence, regardless of the exact moment during the 12-year follow-up, was also evaluated ([Table 2](#tbl2)), given the influence that imbalanced immunosuppression could present on tumor control.

summary.summary:
## Background
- Single-center cohort of 79 adult kidney transplant recipients on tacrolimus were followed for 12 years. Both donors and recipients were genotyped for 37 SNPs across 14 ADME genes.
- Outcomes included survival, tumors, rejection, nephrotoxicity, infections, renal function (eGFR), and tacrolimus pharmacokinetics (dose-adjusted trough, C/D).

## Key Findings
Survival
- Donor ABCB1 rs9282564 AA was associated with lower 12-year mortality (OR 0.116; p=0.029, FDR-adjusted); Kaplan–Meier corroborated better survival vs AG (log-rank p=0.042).
- Donor ABCC2 rs2273697 GA increased mortality risk (OR 4.133; p=0.021, FDR-adjusted); GG showed best survival (log-rank p=0.003).

Tumors
- Donor ABCC2 rs2273697 AA markedly increased tumor risk (OR 13.09; p=0.043 FDR-adjusted).
- Recipient CYP2B6 rs3745274 GT decreased tumor risk (OR 0.099; p=0.048).
- Gene–gene interaction: donor ABCC2 rs2273697 GG plus donor/recipient CYP2C19 rs4244285 AG/AA reduced tumor risk (OR <0.2).

Rejection and renal outcomes
- Chronic rejection: donor ABCB1 rs2235013 GA protective (OR 0.133; p=0.016).
- Acute rejection reduced with recipient CYP3A4 rs2740574 AA (OR 0.080; p=0.047), recipient SLCO1B1 rs4149056 TT (OR 0.157; p=0.024), and donor CYP2B6 rs3745274 GT (OR 0.199; p=0.027); increased with donor UGT1A9 rs6714486 TA (OR 32.1; p=0.020; small numbers).
- Nephrotoxicity reduced with recipient SLCO1B1 rs2306283 AA (OR 0.076; p=0.009) or AG (OR 0.227; p=0.051), donor SLCO1B1 rs2306283 AG (OR 0.108; p=0.024), and donor NOD2 rs2066844 CC (OR 0.015; p=0.035); increased with donor CYP2C19 rs4244285 AA (OR 11.65; p=0.026).
- Re-transplantation risk lower with donor TPMT rs1142345 AA (OR 0.048; p=0.020) and donor CYP2C9 rs1799853 CC (OR 0.102; p=0.042).

Tacrolimus pharmacokinetics (C/D)
- Higher C/D with recipient CYP3A4 rs2740574 AA (p<0.001), recipient CYP3A5 rs776746 *3/*3 (p<0.001), donor CYP2C19 rs4244285 AA (>300 ng/mL/mg/kg after year 3; p=0.026), recipient ABCB1 rs1045642 TT and rs2235033 TT (each p=0.005), and recipient SLCO1B1 rs4149056 TT (p=0.002).
- Lower C/D with donor ABCB1 rs2235013 GG (p=0.011); donor SLCO1B1 rs2306283 genotype influenced early C/D (p=0.01).

Renal function trajectories (eGFR)
- Faster and higher eGFR recovery with recipient CYP3A4 rs2740574 AA (≈60 vs 45 mL/min/1.73 m2; p<0.001), donor CYP3A5 rs776746 *3/*3, recipient CYP2B6 rs3745274 GT; donor CYP2B6 rs3745274 TT had slower recovery (p=0.036).
- Recipient ABCB1 rs1045642 CC and donor ABCC2 rs2273697 GG associated with better eGFR over time (earliest differences from week 1 for ABCC2; p=0.039).

Infections and diabetes
- Infections reduced with recipient ABCB1 rs1045642 CC (OR 0.087; p=0.003), increased with donor ABCB1 rs9282564 AA (OR 23.8; p=0.005).
- Interaction signals: donor CYP2B6 rs3745274 TT + recipient ABCB1 rs2235033 TC increased nephrotoxicity (OR 7.5); donor CYP2B6 rs3745274 TT + donor SLCO1B1 rs2306283 AG increased de novo diabetes (OR 9.8).
- Mortality interactions: recipient CYP3A5 rs776746 GA plus donor ABCB1 rs2235013 GA or donor SLCO1B1 rs2306283 AG increased death risk (each OR 6.4).

## Clinical Implications
- Incorporate combined donor and recipient pharmacogenetic testing into pre- and early post-transplant evaluation, focusing on:
  - Tacrolimus metabolism/transport: CYP3A5 rs776746, CYP3A4 rs2740574, CYP2C19 rs4244285, ABCB1 (rs1045642, rs2235033, rs2235013, rs9282564), SLCO1B1 (rs4149056, rs2306283), ABCC2 rs2273697.
- Use genotypes to tailor tacrolimus dosing and monitoring:
  - Expect higher tacrolimus exposure with recipient CYP3A4 rs2740574 AA, recipient CYP3A5 *3/*3, and donor CYP2C19 rs4244285 AA; consider lower starting doses and closer therapeutic drug monitoring to mitigate nephrotoxicity.
  - SLCO1B1 rs4149056 TT and ABCB1 TT genotypes in recipients associate with higher C/D and lower acute rejection risk; monitor for overexposure.
- Risk stratification and surveillance:
  - Donor ABCC2 rs2273697 (non-GG) flags higher risks (mortality, tumors) and poorer renal trajectories—intensify surveillance.
  - Donor ABCB1 rs9282564 AA increases infection risk; reinforce infection prophylaxis/monitoring.
  - Recipient/donor SLCO1B1 rs2306283 AA/AG and donor NOD2 rs2066844 CC are protective for nephrotoxicity; donor CYP2C19 rs4244285 AA heightens nephrotoxicity risk.
- Consider multi-gene interaction effects when available, as specific CYP–transporter combinations substantially modify risks.
- Findings support CPIC-guided CYP3A5-based dosing and extend utility to additional variants; given the small, single-center cohort, validate in larger, diverse populations before broad implementation.
